uncited: This method performs inverse rendering by optimizing a neural Signed Distance Function (SDF) and shading network to match a target image, using a reparameterization technique that handles boundary gradients exactly.

It differs from approximate differentiable volume rendering methods [4143-single-scattering-differentiable-volume-rendering.md] by computing unbiased gradients for surface boundaries via Monte-Carlo pixel integration, and from differential ratio tracing [4231-differential-ratio-tracing.md] by relying on nested automatic differentiation passes rather than analytical ratio derivations.
It solves the problem of recovering geometry and appearance from images when the underlying representation is a neural implicit surface.
The pipeline optimizes neural network parameters $\theta$ (SDF weights, shading weights, positional encoding biases) to minimize a loss $L$ between the rendered image and a target image.
The rendering is defined by a transformation $T$ from pixel coordinates $u$ to 3D space, modulated by a warp $\mathcal{V}$, and evaluated via the SDF $f$.
- Camera parameters (intrinsics, extrinsics).
- Optimized SDF network $f$ and shading network.
- **SDF Network:** Multi-layer perceptron (MLP).
- For each optimization iteration, select a subset of pixels.
- For each sample, compute the 3D position $x$ via the transformation $T(u, \theta)$.
- Evaluate the SDF $f(x)$ to determine surface intersection.
- Evaluate the shading network at the surface point to get radiance.
- Compute the rendered pixel value by integrating radiance over the pixel samples.
- Update $\theta$ using gradient descent.
- **Silhouette Gradients:** Unbiased derivatives are non-zero only for pixels partially covered by a surface.
Using a subset of pixels makes sampling these pixels rare.
- **Time Complexity:** High due to nested automatic differentiation passes and Monte-Carlo sampling.
- **Measured Performance:** Not given in the sources.
- **When to use:** When recovering high-quality geometry and appearance from images using neural implicit representations is required, and computational resources are sufficient.
- **When not to use:** When real-time performance is required, or when the scene is well-approximated by single-scattering volume rendering.
The method builds on neural SDF representations [Yariv et al. 2020] and geometric network initialization [Atzmon and Lipman 2020].
It addresses the limitations of approximate differentiable rendering methods by providing unbiased gradients for surface boundaries.
